## Claim being audited

Seven configured targets remain covered by `MainProp`, `NashWilliams`, `SuperNW`, `GBetterRelIff`, `Subarr`, `BqoIffGeneralShift`, and `RadoEmbedding`. The uncovered set is unchanged: `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`. The Tablet has nevertheless advanced materially since the previous plan. The universe-generalization task is complete, and `PowerQ`, `PowerChild`, `PowerChildWellFounded`, `PowerSupport`, `PowerSupportNonempty`, `PowerPresentationEq`, `PowerPresentationEqEquivalence`, and `PowerSupportInvariant` now supply the hierarchy core. The recent removal of the two redundant equation-wrapper nodes does not reopen that task. The next missing declaration is genuinely `PowerRel`; there is no lifted order, comparison-game package, hereditary carrier, or target-covering node yet.

The present `PowerQ Q` is the right raw carrier for the route: it has disjoint atom/node constructors, arbitrary nonempty `Type u`-indexed nodes, child well-foundedness, and extensional presentation equivalence. The order may be defined on raw presentations provided it is proved invariant under `PowerPresentationEq` in both arguments. No quotient is required for the preservation proof, but no downstream argument may confuse raw equality with extensional equality. The existing `SetDomination` and `PowerWqoBadPairSequence` belong to the first-level Rado branch and do not attach to any of the three uncovered targets.

The first target must be reached through the manuscript's exact four clauses at lines 1404-1419 and the reflection argument at lines 1533-1550. Negating those clauses yields a canonical one-round Player I response from a failed pair: at a left node choose a child witnessing failure, while at a left atom stay put; every legal response on the right leaves another failed pair. Global classical choices must be functions of the compared presentations, not fresh choices indexed by the input infinite set. Iterating these choices along the shift orbit gives the copied triangular plays. Well-founded child descent proves termination, but termination alone is not enough: the package must prove that the terminal left atom for `X` depends on only finitely many values `h(X), h(Shift X), ..., h(Shift^k X)`. Together with a finite-shift/prefix lemma and local constancy of `h`, that is what proves the reflected map locally constant.

After that reflection theorem, the first covering statement is:

```text
PowerQPresBqo: [IsPreorder Q r] -> Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r).
```

For the hereditary targets, keep the carrier as the induced hereditary part of the full hierarchy. A countably branching tagged code with an erasure into `PowerQ` is a convenient witness; `HereditarilyCountable x` should mean that `x` is `PowerPresentationEq`-equivalent to an erased code. This representation must prove closure under nonempty countable families by choosing codes and reindexing the family by `Nat`; finite families can be repeated. `HerCtblRel r` is then the restriction of `PowerRel r` to the subtype.

There is one necessary refinement to the old converse task. Paper lines 1559-1564 explicitly form the singleton sequence only when the front is nontrivial. If `F = {empty}`, singleton nodes are not in `PrefixTree F`, so an unconditional `ConverseGame` statement is false or ill-typed. State the construction for `empty notin F` (or an equivalent nontriviality condition). In the eventual reverse implication, the deciding front is nontrivial because an empty deciding prefix would make the locally constant multi-sequence constant, contradicting badness and reflexivity. The recursion still needs a new extension-oriented well-founded theorem: on the prefix-tree subtype, `child` is below `parent` when `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. The existing `FrontTreeWellFounded` has the opposite argument orientation and must not drive `TildeF`.

The remaining target statements should be:

```text
BqoHerCtblWqo:   [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellQuasiOrdered (HerCtblRel r)).

BqoHerCtblWellF: [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellFounded
    (fun a b => HerCtblRel r a b and not HerCtblRel r b a)).
```

For the wqo theorem, the forward direction is `PowerQPresBqo`, the elementary `BqoImpliesWqo`, and restriction to the hereditary subtype. The reverse direction passes from a bad locally constant multi-sequence to its deciding-front bad super-sequence, proves that front nontrivial, and applies the hereditary `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded theorem, wqo gives well-foundedness of the strict part via `WellQuasiOrdered.wellFounded`. The converse is special to this hereditary carrier: from a bad sequence `a`, make the countable tail node `T n` containing `a (n+k)`. Reflexivity gives `T (n+1) <= T n`, while badness at index `n` rules out `T n <= T (n+1)`, producing a descending strict chain. Do not use a false general well-founded-implies-wqo principle.

Proceed in the task order below and claim coverage in the order `PowerQPresBqo`, `BqoHerCtblWqo`, `BqoHerCtblWellF`. Existing correspondence or substantiveness debts on unrelated covered branches are verifier work and do not justify reopening the completed universe or hierarchy-core tasks.

Supply usable constructor reduction statements where unfolding is not sufficient. Prove invariance in each argument under `PowerPresentationEq`, using `PowerPresentationEqEquivalence`, and under `[IsPreorder Q r]` prove reflexivity and transitivity and expose a named `IsPreorder` instance on `PowerQ Q`. Keep raw equality distinct from presentation equivalence. Do not import `SetDomination` or `PowerWqoBadPairSequence`, and do not claim a configured target in this layer.

## Claim being audited

The coverage packet shows real progress: `MainProp`, `NashWilliams`, `SuperNW`, `GBetterRelIff`, `Subarr`, `BqoIffGeneralShift`, and `RadoEmbedding` now cover seven configured targets. The six dismissed restriction/Rado tasks have been overtaken and should stay dismissed. The only uncovered targets are `cor PowerQPresBqo`, `thm BqoHerCtblWqo`, and `thm BqoHerCtblWellF`; no hierarchy or hereditary-countability node is present yet. The three open tasks from the prior plan remain mathematically relevant, but they need finer dependency boundaries and one new prerequisite.

The prerequisite is a genuine statement-level blocker. The current declarations `MultiSequence`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `Bqo` quantify their carrier as `Type`, hence universe 0. A faithful PSet-style hierarchy with atoms in `Q : Type u` and arbitrary nonempty `Type u`-indexed nodes lives in `Type (u+1)`. The probe `.trellis/stuck-math-audit/cycle-10-request-63/universe_obstruction.lean` confirms that even for `Q : Type`, the resulting hierarchy relation cannot instantiate the current `Bqo`. The worker must universe-generalize the reused bqo and super-sequence interfaces in place before introducing the hierarchy; a parallel `LargeBqo` would disconnect the target from the existing DAG.

Paper lines 1362-1426 force a tagged well-founded hierarchy, not `Set Q` and not the existing first-level `SetDomination`. Its lifted relation must expose all four clauses: atom/atom is `r`; atom/node is existential on the right; node/atom is universal on the left; node/node is universal-existential. If raw well-founded tree presentations are used, atom and node tags must remain disjoint, and a structural extensional equivalence plus support/relation invariance must be proved before a target node treats the codes as `PowerQ`. Mutual relatedness under `PowerRel Eq` is not an acceptable presentation equality because it equates an atom with a singleton node.

The preservation proof must follow paper lines 1533-1550. Negation of the four-clause relation supplies Player I's choices, but those choices must be canonical functions of the compared hierarchy values. Arbitrarily choosing a strategy separately for every infinite set would not justify local constancy of the reflected map. The finite-game package therefore needs both termination and a finite-dependence theorem for the copied play along the shift orbit. With that in place, the first target attaches directly to the existing `Bqo`, `MultiSequence`, `LocallyConstant`, `BadMultiSequence`, and `ShiftMap` nodes:

```text
PowerQPresBqo: [IsPreorder Q r] -> Bqo r -> Bqo (PowerRel r).
```

For the hereditary targets, define the carrier literally as the induced part of the full hierarchy that has a countable presentation, rather than replacing the full hierarchy by countably branching trees globally. A robust code is a countably branching tagged tree with `Nat`-indexed node children, erased into the full hierarchy; `HereditarilyCountable x` says that `x` is structurally extensionally equal to such an erasure. This handles finite nonempty nodes by repetition and makes closure under arbitrary nonempty countable families provable.

Paper lines 1559-1581 require a second orientation correction. The present Lean signature of `FrontTreeWellFounded` relates a parent to its proper extension, while well-founded recursion defining `TildeF(s)` from values at strict extensions needs the relation `child parent` iff `parent` is a proper initial segment of `child`. The lane packet already marks the current node's correspondence as failed. Do not use that signature for `TildeF`; add an extension-oriented well-founded helper on the prefix-tree subtype. The resulting `ConverseGame` attaches to `Front`, `PrefixTree`, `ProperInitialSegment`, `SuperSequence`, `BadSuperSequence`, the hereditary node-closure lemma, and `PowerRel`.

The final statements should have the following mathematical shape, with `HerCtblRel r` the restriction of `PowerRel r` to the hereditary carrier:

```text
BqoHerCtblWqo:   [IsPreorder Q r] -> (Bqo r <-> WellQuasiOrdered (HerCtblRel r)).
BqoHerCtblWellF: [IsPreorder Q r] ->
  (Bqo r <-> WellFounded (fun a b => HerCtblRel r a b /\ not HerCtblRel r b a)).
```

For the wqo forward direction, use `PowerQPresBqo`, the elementary implication bqo implies wqo, and restriction to the hereditary subtype. For the reverse direction, turn a bad locally constant multi-sequence into its deciding-front bad super-sequence and apply `ConverseGame`. For the well-founded theorem, wqo implies well-foundedness of the strict part by the Mathlib theorem already imported. The converse must use tail nodes of a bad hereditary sequence: the `(n+1)`-tail is below the `n`-tail, while the badness witness at position `n` prevents the reverse relation. This is the paper's countable-subset argument and avoids the false general assertion that well-foundedness alone implies wqo.

Work in the order listed below. The hereditary core may share definitions with the hierarchy package, but target coverage should be claimed in the order `PowerQPresBqo`, then `BqoHerCtblWqo`, then `BqoHerCtblWellF`. Existing correspondence/substantiveness debts on unrelated covered nodes remain verifier work; they are not reasons to reopen the completed restriction or Rado construction tasks.
